newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ABARE forecasts higher Australian beef prices.
newsitem.headline: ABARE forecasts higher Australian beef prices.

text.p: The saleyard indicator price for Australian beef is forecast to rise to 165 cents a kg in 1997/98 to June 30, partly in response to an expected contraction in U.S. beef production, the Australian Bureau of Agricultral and Resources Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.
This compares with ABARE's 1996/97 estimate of 152 cents.

"However, the forecast increase in prices is likely to be tempered by the slow recovery in Japanese and Korean imports of Australian beef and high turnoff rates in Australia," ABARE said in its June quarter commodities review.
ABARE said that at this stage, although the El Nino event was likely to reduce crop yields, sufficient supplies of feedgrains were expected to be available.
Poor pasture conditions in the first four months of 1997 in much of south east Australia and Queensland resulted in high slaughterings, the agency said.
If these conditions continue into the spring a high turnoff of cattle could be expected to continue into 1997/98, it said.

Japanese demand has been slow to recover from the food safety scares of the past year and recent concerns such as the anthrax outbreak in Victoria may contribute to demand remaining relatively subdued, ABARE added.
ABARE is the Australian government's chief commodities forecasting agency.
